AREA FORECAST DISCUSSION
National Weather Service Wakefield VA
315 PM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Chances have increased for SCA conditions on Monday after a
stronger frontal passage. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Unsettled and humid through Sunday as a frontal boundary lifts 
north later today, followed by a cold frontal passage late Sunday. 
Numerous showers, thunderstorms, and localized heavy rain today-
tonight, with scattered showers/storms Sunday.

2) Mainly dry with seasonable temperatures and significantly lower 
humidity Monday-Wednesday. Temperatures warm back above normal late 
in the week an upper ridge builds back into the region.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 315 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Unsettled and humid through Sunday as a frontal 
boundary lifts north later today, followed by a cold frontal passage 
late Sunday. Numerous showers, thunderstorms, and localized heavy 
rain today-tonight, with scattered showers/storms Sunday.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms have started to develop 
across the area, with the most robust convection developing closer 
to the coast in NE NC thanks to the influence of the sea breeze. 
Though the storms are moving slow, they have been moving just enough 
to keep from causing any hydro concerns just yet, however, it is 
still early. The main focal point is a formerly stalled boundary 
starting to lift back northward as a warm front. Current SPC 
mesoanalysis is highlighting PW values of over 2" across SE VA and 
NE NC where the best showers and thunderstorms currently are 
located. Satellite imagery does show some clearing across the 
southern half of the forecast area, so temperatures have been able 
to climb into the mid-upper 80s. Across the northern half of the 
area, temperatures have been generally capped in the lower 80s due 
to the cloud cover, though clouds are starting to clear some, so 
these areas could see temperatures climb a few degrees if this trend 
continues. 

While there is decent instability across the region, the best height 
falls will be later tonight as a shortwave slides through the area. 
With the instability and better support aloft not occuring at the 
same time, the severe threat remains low today, though a few gusty 
showers cannot be ruled out. With high precipitable water values, 
modest instability (skinny CAPE profile), and weak steering flow, 
the environment is favorable for efficient warm rainfall processes 
and localized hydro concerns (supported by an area-wide WPC ERO 
Marginal Risk and a localized upgrade to Slight for portions of the 
I-95 corridor, including metro RIC. Though there is good confidence 
in hydro concerns somewhere across the area, the main question is 
where. This hinges on the movement of the front. Though the event is 
already starting, confidence is too low in any specific location to 
put out a Flood Watch for this afternoon/tonight. Heading into 
tonight, though the best instability does wane overnight, the 
aforementioned shortwave will help provide an additional cold air 
pool aloft that should be sufficient to keep high chc to likely PoPs 
through tomorrow morning. The boundary washes out Sunday, leading to 
noticeably lower convective coverage for the NW 1/2 of the area, but 
high chc to likely PoPs remain in the forecast for the SE and some 
late day storms are still possible in the NW as well. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Mainly dry with seasonable temperatures and 
significantly lower humidity Monday-Wednesday. Temperatures warm 
back above normal late in the week an upper ridge builds back into 
the region.

The upper level flow becomes NW on Monday as a strong upper level 
trough dives SE from the Great Lakes and pushes off the NE and mid-
Atlantic coast Monday night, with an upper level ridge slowly 
expanding NE from the lower MS Valley. This looks strong enough to 
drive the sfc cold front well south of the CWA Monday, and bring 
significantly lower dew points that are more typical of September. 
The models have trended a little farther south and slower with the 
shortwave on Monday, so do expect to see a 3-6 hr window where 
clouds increase and even a few isolated showers develop on Monday 
before the much drier air surges in from the NNW during the 
afternoon (with slight chance PoPs lingering through the
afternoon across the southern areas). 

As high pressure builds in behind the front Monday night, a pleasant 
night is expected Monday night/Tue AM with lows mostly in the upper 
50s to lower 60s (low-mid 50s are likely in many locations to the NW 
of Richmond). The models have trended a bit slower with the return 
flow of moisture so that now dew points look to remain comfortable 
through at least Wednesday as strong sfc high pressure (nearly 1030 
mb), sets up from off the New England coast SW into the Carolina 
coastal plain through midweek. Highs will stay mostly in the low-mid 
80s through Wed with lows in the 50s to lower 60s (locally warmer at 
the immediate coast). The upper level ridge is forecast to expand E-
NE to the TN Valley and central Appalachians Thu-Fri. Temperatures 
climb back to above normal for mid- September, with highs generally 
in the mid-upper 80s. Low end diurnal rain chances return Thu-
Fri.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
As of 205 PM EDT Saturday...

A front is currently situated just to our south, with a mixed bag of 
flight categories across the terminals this afternoon. Most sites 
are reporting MVFR CIGs, though there have been intermittent VFR 
CIGs throughout the day. Showers have started to develop over the 
past hour or so, with ECG and RIC being the main ones impacted. A 
TEMPO is currently in place at ECG, as the convection is more robust 
in this area. RIC has been updated to include VCSH for now. With the 
quick development of showers across the area, the remaining 
terminals will be monitored, and short-term amendments may be 
necessary through the afternoon. This evening, showers and 
thunderstorms become more widespread and confidence is higher, so 
most terminals have a TEMPO group, though timing may need to be 
hedged an hour or two. The widespread SHRA/TSRA gradually 
diminish overnight, but low CIGs likely redevelop between 
06-12Z, especially inland. Winds will generally remain light 
from the southeast this afternoon, becoming southwest tonight. 

Outlook: Remaining unsettled Sunday, though with a lower
coverage of showers/storms than Saturday, with the highest probs
across SE VA/NE NC. Becoming dry and mainly VFR by Monday with 
NE winds, then staying dry Tue-Wed with light winds expect
locally breezy SE VA and NE NC along the coast.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 315 PM EDT Saturday...

Key Messages:

- Generally benign marine conditions are favored this weekend 
  through Sunday night.

- Low-end Small Craft Advisories are possible with increased NE winds
  behind a front late Monday morning through Monday evening.

Early this afternoon, a nearly stationary frontal boundary was 
draped over the far southern coastal waters, extending back into 
the eastern Ohio Valley. This front will slowly lift north this 
evening into Sunday as it weakens. Locally, winds are SSE ~10-15 kt 
south of the front, and mainly E around 10 kt north of it. Onshore 
flow and E-NE wind waves have allowed seas to build to ~3 ft this 
afternoon, with waves 1-2 ft, highest in the far southern portions 
of the Ches Bay.

Winds shift to the E-SE this evening as the front lifts north, then 
veer to S-SW by late this evening/early Sunday. With minimal WAA, 
expect winds to remain ~10 kt overnight, with occasional gusts to 15 
kt. Winds remain SSW 5-10 kt Sunday as the front lifts farther north 
of the local area. Winds do eventually increase ~10-15 kt Sunday 
night ahead of the next frontal passage.

Guidance continues to trend stronger with that front for Monday, 
with better post-frontal CAA on NNE winds Monday afternoon and 
night. Latest local wind probabilities show an uptick for potential 
sustained winds => 18kt in the Ches Bay, with probabilities now in 
the 60 to 90% range late Monday morning into early evening. For 
nearshore coastal waters, high-res guidance shows a 30-50% chance of 
25 kt gusts during that same period. Probabilities and the first 
look at high-res CAM guidance also indicate a brief secondary surge 
is possible Monday night into Tuesday morning, especially in the 
lower Bay and lower James River. WaveWatch and Euro wave guidance 
are a bit more aggressive, which aligns well with the quick ramp-up 
of NE flow late Monday into Monday night. 5-6 ft seas remain 
possible for the southern coastal waters during this timeframe, with 
those 5-6 ft seas potentially lingering in the 20-60 nm offshore 
zones from Monday night into mid-week.

A low risk of rip currents is expected Sunday and Monday.
